cases.title: Paid acquisition plateau at scale
cases.challenge: A mature acquisition system at $450k to $600k a month across search and local services ads. Reporting looked stable while the economics underneath decayed: cost per lead flat, intake-qualified rate falling, case quality down. Leadership read it as execution noise and wanted more budget.
cases.built: Success redefined around intake-qualified cases instead of lead volume. Account structure rebuilt to expose query-level marginal cost. Spend in the protected segments cut by roughly 20 to 25 percent and moved to underfunded intent clusters.
result: Spend settled near $470k to $500k a month
Cost per intake-qualified case improved 25 to 30 percent
Case acceptance returned to its historical baseline
Decisions grounded in economics, not platform optics

cases.title: System noise versus signal
cases.challenge: $180k to $320k a month across paid search, paid social and inbound, with more than 120 tracked KPIs. Fewer than 15 percent correlated with revenue, and 30 to 40 percent of weekly team capacity went to chasing variance with no causal impact.
cases.built: Non-causal metrics removed, cutting tracked KPIs by about 60 to 65 percent. System-level thresholds tied to revenue, retention and intake quality. Initiatives using 20 to 25 percent of capacity with no economic return stopped.
result: Decision speed up while optimization frequency came down
Marketing efficiency up an estimated 18 to 22 percent with no added spend
A system that explains itself under review

cases.title: Disguised winners in paid search
cases.metric: of incremental qualified volume from segments once cut
cases.challenge: Budget moved on 14 to 30 day windows. Some segments swung 30 to 40 percent in weekly cost per acquisition, yet over 60 to 90 days they delivered 1.6 to 2.1 times the downstream value. They kept getting cut.
cases.built: High-variance segments isolated from the core optimization cycle. About 15 to 20 percent of spend protected from short-term suppression. Value judged over a 90 day window.
result: Previously suppressed segments supplied about 30 to 35 percent of incremental qualified volume
Blended cost per acquisition normalized once windows matched downstream economics
Growth stabilized without raising total spend

cases.title: Organizational fear as the constraint
cases.metric: blended acquisition efficiency within two quarters
cases.challenge: Flat or declining growth on more than $3M a year. About 35 to 45 percent of spend sat in initiatives with falling marginal returns, and the structural issues were discussed informally but never reflected in a decision.
cases.built: Fear of being wrong named as a limiting variable. The cost of inaction modeled against re-architecture over 6 and 12 month horizons. Changes phased to protect leadership credibility while restoring function.
result: Blended efficiency up about 18 to 22 percent within two quarters
Decisions based on economics, not narrative defense
